timestamp_derivation: After the closure review demonstrated the inventory-aging defect end to end and the fix was proven against the same replayed attack; before the author timestamp of the commit that introduces this receipt. Per T0091, in the order T0108 requires.

defect_demonstrated.question: Can repeated incomplete sweeps age rooms out of the inventory and wrongly permit stay closures?
defect_demonstrated.demonstration: 60-room property, 60 guests in house. Twelve consecutive sweeps naming only 40 rooms drove the rolling-window inventory 60 -> 40 as the complete sweeps aged out. The thirteenth partial sweep then named 40 of a 40-room building, passed completeness, and closed 20 stays whose guests were still in their rooms.
defect_demonstrated.cause: Completeness was measured against the rooms recent sweeps described, so the evidence being validated also defined the standard. A persistently degraded feed eventually agrees with itself.
defect_demonstrated.impact_if_unfixed: Guests still resident lose network access because their rooms stopped being mentioned.

fix.model: The known room inventory is a PERSISTED FACT per interface, not a rolling observation.
fix.established: Once, from the first uncontradicted sweep.
fix.grows: Only from a sweep that already passed completeness, so a degraded feed cannot enlarge the building either.
fix.shrinks: Only by iam_v2.pms_rebaseline_room_inventory -- an audited operator action requiring an identity and a mandatory reason, recording the removed rooms by name.
fix.cost_accepted: A persistently degraded feed now refuses for ever rather than eventually agreeing with itself. A person has to look. That is the correct cost.

proof.before: 12 partial sweeps -> inventory 40 -> COMPLETED -> 20 in-house stays closed.
proof.after: Same 12 sweeps replayed -> inventory stays 60 -> REFUSED_ROSTER_INCOMPLETE -> 0 closed, all 60 guests keep access.
proof.operator_path: After an audited rebaseline naming the 20 removed rooms, the smaller building reconciles normally and closes the 20.

also_closed: EXECUTE defaults to PUBLIC on a new function, so svc_pmsd could have called the rebaseline and shrunk the building it is measured against. Caught by the migration's own assertion, not by review.
standing_exception: GO_UNKNOWN_STAY remains the documented historical exception in docs/operations/STANDING_PMS_EXCEPTION_GO_UNKNOWN_STAY.md. No stay is fabricated and it is not hidden.
